title: Chris Colfer Reflects on a Healing Glee Reunion as Reboot Talks Continue
excerpt:
Chris Colfer says the standing ovation for his reunion with Darren Criss was unexpectedly moving.
He has discussed returning as Kurt Hummel in the new Glee project, but his participation remains unconfirmed.
seo_title: Chris Colfer on Glee Reunion and Possible Reboot Return
seo_description: Chris Colfer reflects on his Royal Albert Hall reunion with Darren Criss and clarifies his uncertain role in the new Glee project.
body_md:
Chris Colfer has reflected on an emotional reunion that reminded him how much his Glee character, Kurt Hummel, still matters to viewers. Appearing alongside former co-star Darren Criss in London, he found himself facing a much warmer response than he had anticipated. Criss portrayed Blaine Anderson, Kurt's romantic partner, in the musical television series.

The two reunited on October 18, 2026, during Criss's concert at London's Royal Albert Hall and performed Baby It's Cold Outside, a musical callback to their characters' history. Colfer told People that the appearance had been planned for months. He expected an enthusiastic but modest reaction; instead, the audience gave them a standing ovation, making the evening one of the most memorable experiences of his life.

Colfer described the reception as healing. During his years on Glee, he experienced homophobic hostility, and he says the negativity directed at the show after it ended had partly obscured his sense of the positive impact Kurt had made. The response in London offered a powerful reminder that the character had remained meaningful to many people despite the surrounding criticism.

The actor has spoken before about the pressures he faced early in his career. In a 2024 television appearance, he recalled being warned against publicly coming out because it could damage his prospects. His latest comments put the reunion into a broader personal context: it was not simply an opportunity to perform a familiar song, but a chance to see how audiences continued to value a character associated with a formative period of his life.

The conversation arrives as Disney+ and Hulu move ahead with a new Glee project connected to Ryan Murphy's musical comedy-drama. Lea Michele has been reported as returning in the role of Rachel Berry. Colfer's situation is less definite. He has acknowledged conversations about reprising Kurt and said the concept he heard sounded amusing and promising, but he has not confirmed an agreement to appear.

The Royal Albert Hall performance therefore should not be interpreted as a casting announcement for Colfer or Criss. The confirmed developments are their October reunion, Colfer's account of its emotional impact and his discussions about the proposed new series. Whether Kurt Hummel ultimately appears in the revival remains an open question.
